svg.title: Video Super Resolution / Completed and Alternative States
svg.desc: Result layout reference; runtime follows this layout with real committed output. Success requires drain, trailer, flush, close and exclusive final file commit. PLAY RESULT explicitly opens the final file in the existing player. Failed/cancelled tasks never expose partial output as complete. Values are illustrative.

g.text: VIDEO SUPER RESOLUTION
Enhanced video saved
100% / Encoding finalized and output file committed
Final output path / Shared output folder with Merge Videos
/Applications/FluxPlayer/Record/FluxPlayer_SR_20261016_173000_a81f.mp4
Source preserved; no file overwritten. H.264 video re-encoded; audio copied unless AAC selected.
Source 1280 × 720 → Native scale: 2x model 2560 × 1440 → Output 1280 × 720
1800 frames completed / Duration 1m 00s / File size 18.6 MiB / Total time 15m 08s
Inference: CoreML EP (NeuralNetwork fast; may include CPU operators) / Encoder: H.264 libx264 / Audio: original AAC packets / MP4
OPEN OUTPUT FOLDER
PLAY RESULT
Alternative-state specifications (not shown alongside a successful result)
FAILED / UNSUPPORTED CONFIGURATION
Examples: intermediate size limit, encoder limit, disk write failure.
Show failed stage, specific reason and temporary-file cleanup status.
Actions: edit and retry / restart on CPU / back home.
No PLAY RESULT; never change model, resize or skip frames silently.
Runtime EP failure ends the task. CPU retry starts a new full task.
CANCELLING → CANCELLED
Cancelling: wait for safe worker shutdown; disable repeated actions.
Cancelled: show cleanup status; allow reconfiguration or return.
If cleanup fails, show the remaining temporary path, not a result.
No pause / resume or recovery from partially processed output.
Finalizing is still in progress. Show 100% only after successful commit.
